The tale of the Dusk Hollow

Story & Help

Once, the Hollow was never dark

Deep in the bramble valley sits the Dusk Hollow, a forest that never quite falls to night. For as long as anyone remembers, a chain of great glass lanterns kept the gloom at bay — tended, every evening, by the lumenflies: tiny living lights who carried their own glow wherever they went.

Then, one long and starless autumn, the lanterns guttered out one by one. The hollow-beetles — grumpy, armoured things who had always grumbled about the brightness — crept up from the roots and made the dark their home. The lumenflies dimmed and scattered, until only one small light was left flickering on a mossy ledge.

That light is Pip. And Pip has decided that the dark has gone on quite long enough. Lantern by lantern, leap by leap, Pip is going to bring the glow back to the Hollow — if a few cranky beetles get bounced off their ledges along the way, so be it.

How to play

←→  /  AD Run Pip left and right. Let go to glide to a stop. Space  /  ↑  /  W Jump. Hold the button to jump higher; tap it for a little hop. There is a brief moment of grace after you run off a ledge where you can still jump (coyote time), and the game remembers a jump you press just before landing (jump buffering). P  /  Esc Pause and resume the game. R Restart the current level from the start. M Mute or unmute the synthesised sound effects and music. Enter Confirm the highlighted action on any menu (start, next level, retry).

On phones and tablets, use the on-screen ◀ ▶ and ⤒ jump buttons that appear over the game.

What's in a level

  • Lumens — small golden lights. Collect them for points; grab every one in a level for a star.
  • Gems — one rare cyan gem hides off the main path in each world. Worth a big bonus.
  • Beetles — patrol their ledges back and forth. Land on top to stomp them and bounce; touch them from the side and Pip loses a glimmer.
  • Spikes & pits — thorns on the ground and hanging from ceilings, plus bottomless gaps. Any of them costs a glimmer.
  • Checkpoint lanterns — touch one to light it; if you fall, you respawn there instead of the start.
  • Moving platforms — rune-lit slabs that drift on set paths and carry you along. Ride them across gaps and up the brambles.
  • The goal lantern — the big glowing lantern at the end. Reach it to relight it and clear the level.

Pip starts each game with three glimmers (lives). Lose them all and it's game over — but you can retry the level immediately. Clear a level to unlock the next.

Earning stars

  • ★ — finish the level at all.
  • ★★ — also collect every lumen and the gem.
  • ★★★ — also clear it in under 45 seconds.

Design notes — why it feels good

Lumen Leap is written entirely in vanilla JavaScript with the built-in Canvas 2D API. There is no game engine, no framework and no asset files — every sprite, tile, lantern and spark is drawn procedurally with paths and gradients, and every sound is generated live with the Web Audio API. It runs straight from index.html over file://.

The platforming relies on a handful of well-known "good-feel" techniques, all hand-implemented:

  • Fixed-timestep loop with an accumulator, so the physics is deterministic and stable regardless of frame rate.
  • Acceleration & friction on the ground and lighter control in the air, instead of instant velocity, so movement has weight without feeling sluggish.
  • Variable jump height — releasing the jump key early cuts Pip's upward speed.
  • Coyote time and jump buffering — small windows of forgiveness that make jumps land the way you expect.
  • Axis-separated AABB tile collision for clean resolution against the tilemap, plus one-way platforms you can jump up through.
  • A smoothed, bounded camera with a little look-ahead, over a procedurally drawn parallax sky.

Accessibility & comfort

A Calm toggle (and your system's prefers-reduced-motion setting) tones down screen shake, parallax and particles. Sound is fully optional and off-by-one tap away. The whole game is keyboard-playable, and large touch buttons appear on coarse-pointer devices.
